default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vi: Please hang the coat you took off here.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The past-tense verb directly modifies the following noun 「上着」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「を」 marks the direct object receiving the action of hanging (「かける」).
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle 「に」 indicates the place or position where the result of the hanging action is received.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 「かける」 changes to the 「て」 form to connect with the auxiliary verb of request 「ください」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: It follows the verb in the 「て」 form to create a polite request pattern.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.why: The modifying clause 「ぬいだ」 comes before the noun 「上着」 to clarify the object of the action. The place receiving the hanging action is marked by the particle 「に」, together with the polite request pattern 「〜てください」 at the end of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Change it into a request asking the other person NOT to do the action (Please do not hang it here).
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses a much more formal and polite request than 「〜てください」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle 「に」 with 「で」 when indicating a place; for actions of attaching or hanging something somewhere, use 「に」 to indicate the receiving point.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of degree that modifies 「強く」 to increase the intensity of the action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending い changes to 「〜く」 and functions as an adverb modifying the following verb 「おす」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 「おす」 changes to the 「て」 form to combine with the request pattern 「ください」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: It comes at the end of the sentence after the 「て」 form to give a polite request or instruction.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.cn: Aい( remove い ) + く + V / Vて + ください
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.why: The adverb 「もっと」 modifies the changed adjective 「強く」 to form an adverbial phrase of manner. It comes before the verb in the 「〜てください」 form to make a clear, natural request.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Change it into a negative request: “Please do not press any harder.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Change the direct request into advice that the person should press harder.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to change the adjective ending 「い」 to 「く」 when it modifies a following verb. They mistakenly use the basic form 強い押す.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vi: Excuse me, please give me one stamp.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: A word used to get someone's attention or to politely begin a request or purchase.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「を」 marks the item that the speaker wants to receive.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: A counter for thin objects. It comes directly before the predicate to give the quantity of the object being requested.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: A predicate meaning “please give me / please sell me” when it follows a noun and a counter.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.why: The sentence begins with the polite call 「すみません、」, then states the object noun with the particle 「を」, followed by the quantity word 「１まい」, which directly modifies the request action 「ください」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: A more polite and refined way to order food or buy something at a service counter.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Change it into a question asking the price of the stamp instead of requesting the item.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.tip: Learners often put the quantity word in the wrong position, mistakenly saying “１まい切手を” instead of the natural order “切手を１まい”.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.cn: N を + 数量詞 + ください
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vi: My friend drew a map for me.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle 「に」 marks the person who performs the helpful action for the speaker.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「を」 marks the object that is drawn.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 「かく」 changes to the 「て」 form to combine with the auxiliary verb showing that the speaker receives an action 「もらいました」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: A grammar pattern showing that the speaker receives a kind act from another person.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.why: The subject, the speaker, is omitted. The person who performs the helpful action is used with the particle 「に」, and the predicate changes to the 「〜てもらいました」 form to express gratitude for receiving help.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: The subject changes to the friend (友だちが地図をかいてくれました - You drew a map for me).
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It shows that the speaker does something for a friend, rather than being the receiver.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse 「〜てもらう」, where the receiver is the subject and the person doing the action uses に, with 「〜てくれる」, where the person doing the helpful action is the subject and uses が.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.cn: Vて + もらう/もらいます/もらいました
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vi: I will run to the station.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle 「まで」 shows the final destination of the journey.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the 「て」 form modifies the movement verb 「いきます」 and describes the way of moving.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The main predicate of the sentence, describing movement away from the current position.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.why: The particle 「まで」 sets the limit of the destination. The verb 「走る」 changes to the 「て」 form and combines with 「いきます」 to describe moving farther away from the speaker while running.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows movement toward the speaker's position (running from the station to here).
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It simply describes running to the station, without emphasizing movement away from the current position.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the direction of movement between 「〜ていく」, moving away from the speaker's position, and 「〜てくる」, moving toward the speaker's position.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I went to a famous bakery.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: A past-time adverb that sets the time for the whole event in the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending な remains 「な」 when it comes before and modifies the noun 「パン屋」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The suffix 「屋」 forms a noun meaning a shop; the particle 「へ」 shows the direction of movement toward the destination.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The movement verb is changed to the polite past tense 「〜ました」, matching the time reference 「きのう」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.why: The time adverb 「きのう」 at the beginning of the sentence sets the predicate 「行きました」 in the past tense. The adjective 「ゆうめいな」 comes directly before the place noun 「パン屋」 to modify it and is used with the direction particle 「へ」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Use the particle 「に」 instead of 「へ」 to emphasize a specific destination rather than the direction of movement. They are basically interchangeable.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Using the present/future tense would be grammatically wrong because it conflicts with the past time reference 「きのう」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to keep 「な」 when using an adjective ending in な to modify the noun directly after it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vi: I cannot hear the sound of the TV.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の links a modifier to the noun for the sound that comes after it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が is used with the intransitive verb 聞こえる to show the sound that is naturally received through hearing.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The intransitive verb 聞こえる is changed to the polite negative form to say that the sound does not reach the listener's ears.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.why: This sentence describes sound naturally not reaching the ears, so it uses the intransitive verb 聞こえる with the particle が for the thing heard.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows an inability or situation in which one cannot actively listen, unlike 聞こえません, which means that sound naturally does not reach the ears.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particles を and が when they are used with pairs of intransitive sensory verbs such as 聞こえる and 見える.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vi: Because I have an errand, I cannot go to the party.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the existing object used with the verb あります.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form of the verb あります connects clauses and states the cause leading to the result in the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the destination or event that the movement action is directed toward.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 行く changes to the polite negative potential form to show that circumstances make participation impossible.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.why: The first clause uses the て form to state an objective cause. The second uses the negative potential form 行けません to show that circumstances prevent the action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses the subjective decision not to go, rather than being prevented by circumstances as in the potential form 行けません.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.tip: Be careful not to confuse the pronunciation of 用事 (ようじ) with the compound noun 用 (よう) or 幼児 (ようじ - small child).
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vi: I want to hear your opinion.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の identifies possession or the person who formed the opinion.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が is used with the desire ending 〜たい to emphasize the object that the speaker wants to receive.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 聞く combines with the desire ending 〜たいです to politely express the speaker's wish.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.cn: Vます（remove ます） + たい
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.why: The pattern 〜たい expresses the first person's desire. The direct object of the action received usually takes the particle が rather than を.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: It is still grammatical but focuses more on the act of listening, while using the particle が emphasizes the desired object.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.tip: The structure 〜たい is used only to talk about one's own wishes. It is not used directly to ask about the wishes of a superior or a stranger.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the demonstrative pronoun the topic to be evaluated or acted on in the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb 習う is in the polite past tense and expresses something that has been learned or acquired through instruction.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.why: The topic is placed at the beginning with は, followed by the affirmative past predicate 習いました, showing that the learning action from someone has been completed.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It means self-study or the study of general knowledge, while 習いました emphasizes being taught by someone else or practicing a skill.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.tip: Distinguish 習う (learning through an instructor and practicing a skill) from 勉強する (learning general knowledge through self-study).
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vi: Please tell me why you were late.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The short past-form verb acts as a relative clause that directly modifies the noun after it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the noun phrase as the direct object of the action of telling or informing.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The grammar pattern 〜てください attaches to the verb in て form to make a polite request or suggestion.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.why: The short-form verb ちこくした directly modifies the noun りゆう to form an object phrase, followed by the polite request pattern てください at the end of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses a softer and more tactful request than the direct request pattern 〜てください.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.tip: The verb before ください must be changed to the て form. It cannot remain in the dictionary form or the ます form.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vi: Mr. Ou's Japanese pronunciation is very good.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the main topic of the whole comment.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の links a modifier to the noun describing pronunciation.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が identifies the specific part or aspect described by the adjective きれい.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending な serves as the predicate and describes sound quality that is clear and accurate.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.why: The structure は〜が describes a specific part or quality, such as pronunciation, of the main topic being discussed, Mr. Ou.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It emphasizes skill or fluent ability, while きれいです praises a clear, natural, and pleasant sound.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.tip: The quality praised in the structure は〜が must use the particle が. The particle を must never be used before the adjective.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vi: The match was canceled because of the rain.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で shows the objective cause or reason for the event in the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject of a change of state.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に is used with a noun showing the result of a change together with the verb なる.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb なる is in the polite past form and expresses an objective result or decision.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.why: The first clause uses 「N で」 to state an objective cause related to the weather. The second clause uses the change pattern 「N になる」 to show that the match was canceled as a shared decision or natural result.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows a personal choice or decision instead of an objective result such as になる.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.tip: Do not confuse the cause particle で, which is often used with natural disasters, weather, and objective problems, with the means particle.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.cn: N・Aな + になる / Aい (く) + なる
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vi: That bird sings in a very beautiful voice.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative stands before and directly modifies the noun meaning bird.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending な modifies the noun meaning singing voice that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle で shows the means or manner of producing the sound.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb for an animal's call or song is in the polite form.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.why: The sentence begins with the topic 「あの〜は」 to identify the object being observed. It is followed by the manner phrase 「Aな + N で」, which modifies the singing action 「なきます」 at the end.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: The verb なく is an intransitive verb describing an animal's call, so the particle を is not used for the singing voice. Instead, で is used to show the manner.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use the particle を with the verb 鳴く (なく). A sound or voice always uses the particle で to show the manner.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vi: I received a watch from my father for my birthday.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the specific time when the action of receiving the gift took place.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から shows the starting point or the person who gave the gift.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the direct object received.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb もらう is in the polite past form and expresses that the speaker received something from someone.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.why: The giving-and-receiving structure 「N (giver) から/に + N (thing) を + もらう」 expresses who the speaker received something from and what it was. It can be combined with the time phrase 「N に」 at the beginning.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If くれました is used, the giver, such as the father, must be the subject connected to が/は, instead of using the particle から.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses the opposite direction: the speaker gave the watch to the father instead of receiving it from him.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.tip: With the verb もらう, the subject is the receiver, understood as “I.” The giver uses に or から. Do not confuse this with the structure くれる.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vi: Many people are gathering in the park.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the destination or place where the gathering takes place.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject of the intransitive verb 集まる.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The quantity adverb directly modifies the degree of the gathering action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The intransitive verb 集まる in the 〜ている form describes the resulting state in which many people are present together.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.why: The verb 集まる is an intransitive verb meaning to gather at a place, so it uses the particle に for the place and が for the people. The ending 〜ている describes a state continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Do not use the particle で with a verb describing gathering at one point, such as 集まる. Use に instead.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: This is a transitive verb meaning to collect something, where the subject causes the object to form a group (Nを).
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.tip: The verb 集まる (gather) is intransitive and uses the particles に (place where people gather) and が (people who gather). It differs from 集める, which is transitive and uses the particle を.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vi: Someday I want to become a doctor.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb for an unspecified future time that modifies the following expression of desire.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に combines with the verb なる to show the result of a change or a goal.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb なる changes to the たい form to express the speaker's wish, and です is added to make it polite.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.why: The sentence expresses a future dream. The adverb いつか modifies the predicate なりたい, while the occupation noun いしゃ uses the particle に to show the result of the change.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Use it to express the speaker's wish for someone else to do something, while たい expresses the speaker's own wish.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Use it to express a third person's desire. Do not use it for the speaker's direct desire.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use the particle を instead of に before the verb なる.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vi: Every evening, I prepare for the lesson in advance.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A repeated-time adverb at the beginning of the sentence sets the background for a habit.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects two nouns and modifies the content being prepared.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the action する.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb する is in the polite form and expresses a regular daily action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.why: The sentence describes a daily habit: the repeated-time adverb 「まいばん」 comes first, followed by the object phrase 「N の N を」 and the action predicate 「します」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It means reviewing an old lesson after class, the opposite of よしゅう, which means preparing a new lesson before class.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.tip: Distinguish 予習 (よしゅう — preparing a lesson before class) from 復習 (ふくしゅう — reviewing a lesson after studying it).
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vi: When speaking with someone you meet for the first time, use polite language.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The adverb modifies the following verb meaning “meet.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the following noun meaning “person.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle と indicates the person who participates in the conversation.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the noun indicating the time とき.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は emphasizes the situation or circumstances as the topic for the advice in the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective ending な modifies the following noun meaning “language.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of using.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: The verb ending 〜ましょう is used to make a polite invitation or suggestion.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.why: The subordinate clause 「〜ときは」 identifies the circumstances and contains the embedded modifier 「はじめて会う人」; the main clause ends with the inviting ending 「〜ましょう」 to encourage proper behavior.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It directly asks the listener to do something instead of inviting both people to do it together, as in ましょう.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses strict obligation (“must use”) instead of a polite suggestion.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.tip: A clause modifying a noun とき always uses the plain form; here, the dictionary form 話す shows an action that happens at the same time or in the future.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた・Aい・Aな・Nの ＋ とき
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vi: On days off, I often read novels.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: It modifies the following noun by specifying its time-related quality.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は, together with the comma, makes the time expression the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The frequency adverb directly modifies the verb meaning “read” at the end of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を identifies the object affected by the action of reading.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The predicate is a verb in the polite form and expresses a usual habit.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.why: The time topic 「やすみの日は」 is moved to the beginning to set the context, the adverb 「よく」 comes before the object or verb to show frequency, and the particle 「を」 directly connects the object with the action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows almost absolute frequency (always, every time), while 「よく」 means only often.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It shows lower frequency (sometimes, occasionally), and does not mean “often” like 「よく」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the position of frequency adverbs such as 「よく」 or forget to use the particle 「を」 before a transitive verb.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vi: There is no one who knows how to use it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the object of the verb expressing understanding わかる.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The basic-form verb creates a clause modifying the noun 人 immediately after it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The head noun, modified by the preceding clause, serves as the topic with the particle は.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The question word combines with the particle も and a negative predicate to make a complete negation.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The predicate expresses the existence of a person in the polite negative form.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 ＋ も ＋ Negative-form verb (Vない / Vません)
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.why: The phrase 「つかいかたが わかる」 acts as a modifier for 「人」 and forms the sentence topic; the complete negative structure 「だれも＋negative」 emphasizes that there is no one at all.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It indicates an unspecified person (someone), and usually appears in affirmative sentences or questions rather than complete negation.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses complete affirmation (anyone), and usually appears in an affirmative sentence meaning that anyone can do it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.tip: Avoid confusing the particle 「を」 with 「わかる」 because this verb expresses a state or ability and requires 「が」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the subject performing the action in the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of caring for or growing.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb そだてる in the ています form expresses an activity that continues as a habit or job.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.why: The sentence follows the order Subject (父は) - Object (やさいを) - Predicate (そだてています), where the transitive verb 「そだてる」 takes the ending 「〜ています」 to express work that continues over time.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It is an intransitive verb (grow, develop), so the subject must be a plant or child and go with 「が」; do not use 「を」 for the person who grows it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the intransitive verb 「そだつ」 (grow by itself) with the transitive verb 「そだてる」 (raise, grow).
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の modifies the noun “party” by specifying its time.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the noun that identifies the content of the preparation.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を makes the noun “preparation” the object of the verb.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb する takes the ending ましょう to invite someone or actively suggest doing an action together.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.cn: Vます (remove ます) ＋ ましょう
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.why: Two nouns are connected successively by 「の」 to form a complete object phrase 「あしたのパーティーのようい」, which combines with the suggestion ending 「〜ましょう」 to invite the other person to do it together.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It is a request or command for the listener to do something (please do it), and does not express doing it together like 「しましょう」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It is a polite invitation that checks the other person’s opinion (will you do it too?), with a gentler inviting tone.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.tip: When several nouns are connected by the particle 「の」, translate backward from the core noun at the end (ようい) to the beginning.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vi: The coffee I made is very delicious.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が indicates the subject who performed the action of making coffee in the modifying clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The short past-form verb directly modifies the noun コーヒー before it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: After being modified by the preceding clause, the head noun becomes the main topic with the particle は.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending い combines with です as a predicate that evaluates quality.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nの ＋ N (Clause modifying a noun)
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.why: The subject in a relative clause must use the particle 「が」 (わたしが), and the verb uses the plain form 「いれた」 to modify the noun 「コーヒー」, making the entire phrase the topic with 「は」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: This is grammatically incorrect because, in a clause modifying a noun, the subject cannot use the particle 「は」 and must use 「が」 instead.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use the particle 「は」 instead of 「が」 for the subject inside a clause modifying a noun.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vi: I am busy that day (it is inconvenient), so another day would be better.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative modifies the noun meaning “day” immediately after it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the time point the topic of the reason clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が goes with つごう as the subject of the adjective わるい.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The conjunction ので connects a clause expressing an objective reason and is followed by a comma for a pause.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The phrase modifies the noun 日 and means “another day.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle が marks the object being chosen or evaluated before the adjective いい.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: The adjective いい combines with です as a predicate expressing a wish or suggestion.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.why: The first clause uses the conjunction 「ので」 after the adjective 「わるい」 to present the reason objectively and politely. The second clause uses the particle 「が」 before 「いいです」 to suggest a more suitable option.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: It also expresses a reason, but is more subjective and emotional, and less polite than 「ので」 when refusing or arranging a schedule.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.tip: When connecting a noun or an adjective ending な with 「ので」, you must add 「な」 (for example: 休みなので, ひまなの​​で) instead of using 「だ」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな (な)・N (な) ＋ ので
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vi: I do not like apples as much as strawberries.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the noun りんご the topic being compared.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle ほど is used with the noun that sets the comparison standard and combines with a negative predicate to show that something is not equal in degree.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in な is changed into the polite negative form and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.why: The pattern for a less-than comparison, N1 は N2 ほど ... ない, uses N2 as the higher comparison standard to show that N1 does not reach that level.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It directly states that N2 is greater than N1, while the original pattern emphasizes that N1 does not reach N2’s level.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.tip: The grammar pattern ほど, which expresses a less-than comparison, must be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.cn: N ＋ ほど ＋ Vない形・Aくない・Aではない
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vi: I am working at a hospital.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the topic and the subject performing the action in the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place or organization to which the speaker belongs or where the speaker works.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb つとめる is changed into the ている form to express a stable, long-term work status or occupation.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.why: The verb つとめる means working as an employee belonging to an organization, so it must be used with the particle に to indicate the workplace.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It only describes work taking place at a location (using で), while つとめる (using に) emphasizes membership in that organization.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle で with the verb つとめる. The correct usage is につとめる.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vi: Please let me take a picture of this painting.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative directly modifies the noun え that follows it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun combines with the particle の to modify the noun しゃしん.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the direct object affected by the action of taking a picture.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.3.vi: please let me take a picture
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb とる is changed into the causative て形 form and combined with ください to create a pattern asking the other person for permission to perform the action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.why: The pattern Vさせてください uses the causative form together with ください to express the speaker’s wish to ask the listener for permission to perform the action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used to ask the listener to perform an action, while させてください asks for permission for the speaker to do it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This is an ordinary request for permission, while させてください has the nuance of asking the listener to allow or help make it possible for the speaker to do something.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.tip: Do not confuse とってください, which asks someone else to take a picture, with とらせてください, which asks permission for the speaker to take it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.cn: V使役形 て形 ＋ ください
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: This polite demonstrative pronoun combines with the particle を to mark the object being looked at.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The special honorific form of the verb みる combines with the question particle か to ask politely about the listener’s action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.why: The sentence uses the formal demonstrative こちら and the special honorific form ごらんになる to show politeness and respect toward the other person.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This is the humble form used for the speaker’s own act of looking or seeing. It must not be used to ask about the listener’s action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This is the passive or ordinary potential honorific form. It is less formal than ごらんになる.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.tip: Do not confuse the honorific form ごらんになる, used for the other person, with the humble form はいけんする, used for oneself.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.cn: N を ＋ ごらんになる
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vi: I am right in the middle of doing my homework.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the direct object affected by the action of doing homework.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The progressive verb form ている directly modifies the formal noun ところ that follows it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: This sentence-final grammar pattern shows that an action is happening at that exact moment.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.why: This pattern combines the progressive form ている with the formal noun ところ to emphasize the exact time when the action is happening now.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows the moment just before starting to do the homework.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It shows the moment just after finishing the homework.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.tip: Pay attention to the verb form before ところ: the dictionary form means “about to do,” V-ている means “be doing,” and the V-ta form means “have just done.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vている・Vた形 ＋ ところだ
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The stem of the intransitive verb 聞こえる describes sound naturally reaching the listener’s ears.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The ending used by Group 2 verbs in the dictionary form at the end of a sentence or word.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t5-q1.kobun.why: The word “聞こえる” is a Group 2 intransitive verb meaning that sound naturally reaches the ears. It is often used with the particle が to mark the sound being received.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If the transitive verb 聞く is used with the particle を, it means actively listening or asking.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If the potential form 聞ける is used, it expresses having the opportunity, time, or conditions to listen.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t5-q1.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse 聞こえる, meaning that sound naturally reaches the ears and used with が, with 聞ける, meaning that one has the ability or conditions to listen.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vi: On Sundays, I study at home, but sometimes I also go out with my friends.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the time and topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place where the studying takes place.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ～ています describes an action in progress, while が connects it to the contrasting idea that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle と indicates the person performing the action together with the subject.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The dictionary-form verb combines with こと to turn the action into a noun; も adds the meaning “also.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: あります completes the pattern ～こともあります and expresses that something sometimes also happens.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.why: The sentence first states the activity that usually happens, then uses が to shift to another activity that may also happen. と indicates the person going together, while こともあります turns the action 出かける into “going out” and emphasizes “sometimes also.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～ことがある, the meaning is still “have done before/sometimes,” but it does not emphasize “also.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often omit こと when they want to turn a verb into a noun in the pattern ～こともあります.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ こともある
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vi: Because I had a stomachache, I had not eaten anything since morning.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks おなか as the body part that is painful.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form of the adjective いたい connects the reason to the action that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates the starting point of a period of time.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 何も combines with the negative form to mean “nothing at all.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: Vないで connects the omitted action with the continuing state.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: いた is the past form of いる and shows that the state of not eating continued during that period.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.why: いたくて gives the reason before the result. 何も combines with 食べないで to negate the whole object, while いた describes a continuing state.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with this form, the meaning is still “not do,” but the tone is more formal and stiff.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.tip: 何も must be used with a negative form; do not use 何も食べていた to say “not eat anything.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q10.tokens.9.m: was/were staying; was/were in the state of
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.cn: Aいくて; Vないで + いる
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vi: When I arrived at the classroom, the class had already started.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the destination of the action 着く.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: Vたら connects a condition or an earlier time with the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks じゅぎょう as the subject that starts.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: Vていました describes a state that happened and continued to exist at the mentioned time.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.why: 着いたら sets the time reference for observing the state of the class. はじまっていました shows that the starting happened before the speaker arrived.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would focus on a natural result or something that happens every time one arrives at class.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.tip: Vたら here does not mean the hypothetical “if”; it means “when one has arrived.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.cn: Vた・Aい・Aな・Nだった + ら; Vている + ました
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vi: I came home late at night and made my father angry.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: 夜 is a time phrase placed at the beginning of the sentence to give the time background.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: おそい modifies 時間, while に marks the time when the action 帰る happened.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects action 帰る with the next action in before-and-after order.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the person affected by the causative structure.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: おこらせました is the polite past form of the causative structure, describing making the father angry.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first and before the verb to show when the action happened. 帰って connects to the following clause, while 父を marks the person made angry in the causative structure.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, it means that the father became angry by himself, without emphasizing that the speaker caused it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If this passive pattern is used, it means that the speaker was scolded by the father or that the father became angry with the speaker.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse を in the causative structure with を used for an ordinary object, but here を marks the person affected.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.cn: Vる → Vさせる; Vない → Vさせない; Vた → Vさせた; Vて → Vさせて
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vi: Could you return the book you lent me last week?
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.sk: Time に + Vた + N を + Vて + もらえませんか
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: 先週 shows the time when the action of lending the book happened.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense clause modifies 本, creating the meaning “the book that was lent.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the book as the object being returned.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 返して connects the main verb with the requesting pattern てもらえませんか.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.4.vi: could you do it for me
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: もらえませんか expresses a polite request, meaning “could you do it for me?”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning, followed by a clause modifying 本. 本を marks the thing being returned, while 返してもらえませんか is used to politely ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced here, the sentence becomes a more direct and less gentle request than てもらえませんか.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern asks for permission to do something; it does not ask someone else to do it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake てもらえませんか for a question about ability, but in this sentence it is mainly a polite request.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.cn: Vて + もらえませんか
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vi: The war that lasted for ten years finally ended.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.sk: Period of time も + Vた + N が + Vた
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: も emphasizes that the period lasted for a notably long time.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 続いた is in the past form and modifies せんそう, meaning “the war that lasted.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the war as the subject that ended.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 終わった is the main predicate in the past form.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.why: The period 年も is placed first to emphasize the duration, followed by the clause 続いた modifying せんそう. The subject of the ending action is marked by が.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If も is removed, the sentence only states that it lasted ten years, without emphasizing the feeling that it was very long or surprising.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means about ten years, showing an estimated number instead of emphasizing the duration.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.tip: Do not translate も in this sentence as “also”; with periods of time, も usually has the feeling of “as much as” or “for the whole time.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vi: Thinking about my child's future, I make my child study even during the summer vacation.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども with しょうらい, showing possession or a related object.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the child's future as the object being thought about.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 考えて connects the reason or basis for thinking with the action in the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: でも expresses concession: the child still studies even during the vacation.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: 勉強させて is the て causative form, connected to います to describe continuing to make the child study.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: います follows the verb in the て form to show that a state or action is continuing.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.why: しょうらいを考えて gives the basis for the main action. 夏休み中でも creates the concessive meaning, while 勉強させています shows that the subject continues making or letting the child study.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If でも is replaced with は, the sentence only states the time of the summer vacation and no longer has the meaning “even while on vacation.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only says that the child is studying; it does not show that someone makes or lets the child study.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.2.d: This pattern emphasizes that the speaker asks for or receives help through the child's studying, which differs from the causative meaning of させる.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may overlook the causer: 勉強させる does not only mean “study” but means “make or let someone study.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.cn: V使役: Vさせる; Vさせて+いる; N+でも
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vi: I was taught Japanese by my teacher.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person who performs the action of helping or teaching the speaker.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the content being taught.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the verb 教える with いただく to create a polite way of saying that one received help.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: いただきました expresses the speaker's humble statement that they received help.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.why: The person receiving help is the unspoken subject of the sentence, and the helper is marked by に. The content being taught goes with を, and then 教えて connects with いただきました using the て form.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてもらう is used, it still means receiving help, but the polite and humble tone is weaker.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてくださる is used, the focus shifts to the other person willingly doing it as a favor.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may put に in the wrong position and forget that the person receiving help is usually the unspoken subject of ～ていただく.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vi: Because this book has large writing, even people with poor eyesight can read it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.sk: N は + N が + Aい ですから、+ N が + Aい + N でも + potential V
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes this book the topic being explained.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks a specific feature of the book.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ですから connects the reason clause with the result that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the subject that has the negative feature.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective 悪い comes before 人 to modify a person with poor eyesight.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: でも means “even,” expanding the group of people who can still read.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: 読めます is the potential form, expressing the ability to read the book.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.cn: Potential V + ます; Aい + ですから; Aい + N; Nでも
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason based on the book's feature, and then ですから leads to the result. The clause 目が悪い modifies 人, while でも emphasizes that even this group can read it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ですから is replaced with ～ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～ても is used, the meaning is “even though one's eyesight is poor,” emphasizing concession instead of limiting the group with でも.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake が in 目が悪い for a particle linking two sentences, but here it marks the subject of the adjective 悪い.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vi: A: I am a little tired, aren't I? B: Then, shall we take a break?
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: 少し modifies the degree of tiredness.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.1.vi: a little tired, aren't I; then
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 疲れました is the predicate of the first utterance; ね asks for agreement, while じゃあ moves on to the next suggestion.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the state or activity chosen after しましょう.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ～ましょうか is used to make a suggestion or politely ask for someone's opinion.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.cn: N にする; Vます remove ます ＋ ましょうか
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.why: Speaker B uses the situation mentioned in the previous sentence to make a suggestion. に marks the choice “take a break,” while ～ましょうか turns the sentence into an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～ましょう is used, the suggestion sounds more decisive and does not directly ask for an opinion with か.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate にする as “do,” but in this sentence it means choosing or changing to the state of taking a break.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vi: Whenever my younger sister sees sweets, she always wants to eat them.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the younger sister as the topic.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks what is seen.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ～ると connects a natural condition or time with a result that usually occurs.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: いつも modifies 食べたがる and shows how often the desire occurs.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ～たがる is used to express another person's desire; here, the subject is the younger sister.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ と; Vます remove ます ＋ たがる
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.why: 見つると creates a relationship in which “when the first action happens, the following result usually occurs.” Because the person who has the desire is the younger sister, the sentence uses 食べたがる instead of directly using 食べたい.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 食べたい, the sentence expresses the speaker's own desire.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～たがっている is used, it emphasizes the desire that is being shown at the moment of speaking.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 食べたい for other people, but when expressing another person's desire, they need to use ～たがる or ～たがっている.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vi: I will work hard so that I can soon be useful to everyone.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.sk: Vたい adverb ＋ Nの ＋ Nに ＋ potential V ＋ ように ＋ Vます
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: はやく modifies the effort action and shows the desired manner or time.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects みなさん with the phrase 役に立てる to identify the person who will benefit.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 役に立てる expresses the ability to become useful or help someone.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ように connects a goal with the action がんばります and is often used before a desired ability or state.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: がんばります is the main action performed to achieve the goal stated earlier.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.cn: potential V・Vない ＋ ように; Nの ＋ ように; Vます remove ます ＋ ように
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.why: The phrase みなさんの役に立てる expresses the goal of being able to help everyone. ように connects this goal to がんばります, while はやく shows the wish to achieve the goal soon.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～ために is used, the purpose is more active and shows a clearer intention; ように is suitable for a goal involving ability.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use ～ために for every purpose, but before a potential verb such as 立てる, ～ように is usually used.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vi: A: When are you going out? B: I will go out after taking a shower.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: いつ asks when the action 出かける occurs.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 出かけますか creates a polite question about going out.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks シャワー as the object of あびる.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: Vたあとで connects an earlier action with the next action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.why: いつ comes before the predicate to ask about the time. The clause あびたあとで states the action completed first, followed by 出かけます.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes going out before taking a shower.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse あとで with 前に and reverse the before-and-after order.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vi: You must not enter the temple while still wearing a hat.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks ぼうし as the item being worn.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: Vたまま expresses keeping the same state after performing an action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of the action 入る.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 入って connects the verb 入る with the prohibition pattern that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてはいけません expresses something that is prohibited.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.why: かぶったまま describes the state accompanying the action 入って. The pattern 入ってはいけません places the prohibition at the end of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence emphasizes entering the temple without wearing a hat, not keeping the same state.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.tip: Do not understand まま as simply meaning “after”; this pattern emphasizes that the state remains unchanged.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.cn: Vた・Nの ＋ まま; Vて ＋ はいけない
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vi: Since we will use this room from now on, please turn on the lights in advance.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces この部屋 as the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the time when use begins.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason with the request in the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks 電気 as the object being turned on.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects the action of turning on the lights with おく.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: Vておいてください asks someone to do something in advance to prepare for a later purpose.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.why: The clause 使うので gives the reason before the request. おいてください shows that turning on the electricity must be completed first so that the room is ready.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with this, it only means “please turn on the electricity,” without emphasizing preparation in advance.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out おく and lose the meaning of “do it in advance for later use.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので; Vて ＋ おく; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vi:
Tanaka: 「Yamashita, you look down. What happened?」
Yamashita: 「Actually, my girlfriend just told me to break up with her.」
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The first speaker’s name begins the dialogue turn.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The familiar form of address くん is used with a comma to attract the other person’s attention.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject of the adjective describing the state ない.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The negative adjective ない combines with the modal particle ね to make a gentle comment and seek agreement.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The phrase asking about the reason どうした combines with the particle の to form a casual question that ends Tanaka’s turn.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The second speaker’s name begins the reply explaining the reason.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: An opening adverb used to reveal a private reason or a difficult truth.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle に marks the agent performing the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.8.vi: to say, “Please break up with me”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.8.n: The request form of the verb てくれ combines with the quotation particle と to directly quote the content of the request.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.9.n: The passive verb 言われた combines with the explanatory ending んだ to explain why the speaker feels down.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.why: The first turn uses the phrase '元気がない' to describe the person’s appearance and 'どうしたの' to ask about them casually. The reply uses the passive form '〜に…と言われた' with 'Vてくれと' to express being asked by someone else to do something, ending with 'んだ' to explain the reason for the speaker’s low mood.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 別れてほしいと is used, it more indirectly quotes the wish “I want to break up.”
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If the imperative form 別れろと is used, the speech sounds harsher, ruder, and more forceful.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.tip: When quoting the other person’s request in the passive sentence '〜に…と言われた', use the request form '〜てくれ' instead of confusing it with '〜てあげる'.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ くれ ＋ と ＋ 言われる
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vi: It is cold today, so why don’t you try wearing gloves?
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks 今日 as the time topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The conjunction から shows that the cold weather is the reason for the suggestion in the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of putting something on one’s hands.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The conditional form of the verb たら provides a condition for making a suggestion.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern どうですか is used to give a gentle suggestion or piece of advice.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.why: The first clause uses から to give the cold weather as the reason. The second clause uses Vたらどうですか to give gentle advice or suggest an action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It is more direct and somewhat more decisive than the gentle suggestion of 〜たらどうですか。
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It asks or requests the other person to perform an action, rather than suggesting an option.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the verb used with gloves (手袋をする) with verbs such as 着る or はく.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vi: You know that smoking is not allowed here, right?
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で marks the place where the prohibited action takes place.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を identifies the object affected by the action of smoking.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern てはいけない expresses a rule prohibiting an action.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: Use という to quote and explain the specific content of the noun こと.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the entire nominalized clause as the object of the verb 知る.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The stative predicate 知っています combines with the modal particle よね to confirm information with the listener.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.why: The sentence uses ということ to package the entire prohibition clause 「ここでタバコを吸ってはいけない」 as a noun phrase that functions as the object of 知っています, ending with よね to seek agreement or confirmation.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used to end a direct prohibition politely. It is not used to modify the noun こと inside a larger phrase as in the usual pattern いけない.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It is used directly after an ordinary noun, but when saying that someone knows a fact or clause, nominalization through ということ is required.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to change the predicate to the plain form before ということ, or mistakenly use the particle が instead of を before 知っています.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ はいけない / 普通形 ＋ という ＋ N
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vi: A: "Has Mr. Tanaka come back yet?" B: "I will go to the room to take a quick look and come right back."
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks Mr. Tanaka as the topic of Speaker A’s question.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb もう emphasizes whether an action has been completed by the present time.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The conjugated verb 〜てくる expresses the action of returning to this place, together with the question particle か.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The adverb ちょっと indicates that the trip to take a look will be brief.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle まで marks the endpoint of the movement.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.5.vi: go and take a look, then come back right away."
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern V(remove ます) + に行く combines with 〜てくる to express going somewhere for a purpose and then returning to the original place.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.why: Speaker B uses V(remove ます) + に行く to show the purpose of the movement (going to take a look), combined with the ending 〜てきます to show that they will return to the place where the conversation is taking place after looking.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It only indicates movement away from the speaker’s location, without implying a return, unlike 〜てきます.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It only expresses the ordinary action of looking at something in the current place. It does not show movement to another place for the purpose of looking, as in 〜に見に行きます.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse 〜ていきます (going away without returning) with 〜てきます (going to do something and then returning to the original place).
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.cn: Vstem ＋ に ＋ 行く / Vて ＋ くる
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vi: Are there any classes where I can speak a lot of Japanese?
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the language object of the action of speaking.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb たくさん modifies the degree of the verb 話す.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 話す is nominalized with こと and combines with the particle が as the object of ability.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The ability verb できる acts as the predicate of the clause modifying the following noun クラス.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は makes the noun クラス the topic in a question about existence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb あります expresses the existence of an inanimate thing and combines with the question particle か.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.why: The clause 「日本語をたくさん話すことができる」 uses Vることができる to modify the noun クラス. It then uses the particle は to make the class the topic and asks about its existence with ありますか.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Use the direct ability form instead of the phrase ことができる. The meaning is the same, but it is shorter and more conversational.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It only means “a class that speaks Japanese” as an ordinary habit or action. It does not emphasize the ability or opportunity to speak, as the ability pattern does.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to put the verb in the dictionary form before ことができる and incorrectly change it to the ます form or the て form.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ことができる
